check.title: Male reproductive structures and the sperm pathway

mc.prompt: Which sequence correctly follows sperm after they leave the epididymis?
mc.cue: Trace connected transport ducts, not every nearby organ.
mc.explanation: Sperm pass through the vas deferens and ejaculatory duct before entering the urethra.

mc.prompt: Which statement distinguishes sperm from semen?
mc.answer: Semen contains sperm mixed with accessory-gland secretions
options: Sperm are the fluid secreted by the prostate
Sperm and semen name exactly the same material
Semen is produced only by interstitial cells
Semen contains sperm mixed with accessory-gland secretions
mc.cue: One term names a cell; the other names a mixture.
mc.explanation: Sperm are reproductive cells. Semen is the mixture of cells and gland secretions.

writing.prompt: Trace the sperm pathway from its production site to the outside. Include where maturation occurs.
writing.model: Sperm form in seminiferous tubules, enter the epididymis for maturation and storage, then move through the vas deferens, ejaculatory duct and urethra to the outside through the penis.
criteria: Names production and maturation sites correctly.
Places the major transport ducts in order.

writing.prompt: Explain why a blocked vas deferens could prevent sperm from appearing in semen without stopping all semen production.
writing.model: The duct blockage interrupts sperm transport. Seminal vesicles, the prostate and bulbourethral glands add secretions through other connections. Some gland fluid can still enter the downstream pathway.
criteria: Does not infer loss of testosterone solely from a blocked duct.

worked.label: Worked example
worked.title: A blocked transport duct
worked.scenario: A model shows normal seminiferous tubules and accessory glands but a completely blocked vas deferens.
steps: Start at the production site. The seminiferous tubules may still produce sperm.
Follow the route. Sperm cannot pass the blockage to reach the ejaculatory duct.
Consider the glands separately. Their ducts may still add fluid downstream.
Predict carefully: the ejaculate can contain gland fluid without sperm. The blockage does not itself establish that testosterone production has stopped.

guided.label: Practise with support
guided.title: Apply the explanation
guided.instruction: Try both questions. Use the hint to revise your thinking after an incorrect answer.

items.prompt: After sperm mature in the epididymis, which major duct carries them toward the ejaculatory duct?
items.hint: Follow the route out of the testis region.
items.explanation: The vas deferens is a transport duct carrying sperm from the epididymis toward the pelvic ducts.

items.prompt: A seminal-vesicle secretion contains fructose. Which function does this support?
items.answer: Providing an energy source for sperm
options: Providing an energy source for sperm
items.hint: Separate gland secretions from the cells made in the testis.
items.explanation: Fructose in the secretion supplies a usable energy source; sperm production occurs in seminiferous tubules.

new_optional_model: Newly produced sperm cannot pass through the interrupted epididymides to reach the downstream sperm ducts. Accessory-gland fluid still has its own downstream entry points, so it need not disappear. This prediction concerns new transport after the interruption; it does not determine whether sperm were already stored farther along before it occurred. Unlike the worked example, this model changes a cell-transport route rather than only the composition of a gland secretion.
